note: Practice texts are reading material for Lilt's exercises and Studio. Levels follow the NHS Fife progression order (automatic speech first, then longer and more spontaneous speech). Only move up when the current level feels comfortable and consistent.

levels.title: Warm-ups
levels.subtitle: Hums and gentle glides
levels.basis: NHS Fife: humming gently on a comfortable pitch, and gentle pitch glides as a warm-up.

items.text: mmmmmmm
items.hint: Hum gently on a comfortable note for a few seconds. Notice where you feel it.

items.text: mmmmmmm
items.hint: Hum again, aiming the sound forward until your lips tingle.

items.text: mmm ↗ ↘
items.hint: A gentle glide: slide a little up and back down, like a soft siren. Easy, never strained.

items.text: mmmee · mmmaa · mmmoo
items.hint: Start with the hum and let it open into each vowel.

levels.title: M and N words
levels.subtitle: Keep the buzz forward
levels.basis: NHS Fife: short words starting with m, holding the m a little longer at first. You can make up your own.
levels.written_by: First list from the source; other lists written by Lilt in the same pattern.

items.text: meet · many · maybe · Mary · magic
items.hint: Hold the m a little longer at first.

items.text: moon · mellow · mild · morning · mine
items.hint: Feel the m on your lips before the vowel.

items.text: name · nine · near · noon · new
items.hint: The n buzzes just behind your top teeth.

items.text: mini · money · meaning · mimic · mango
items.hint: Two m's in some words: keep both forward.

levels.title: Automatic speech
levels.subtitle: Things you don't have to think about
levels.basis: NHS Fife progression: start with speech you don't have to think about (counting, days, months), so you can focus on how you sound.

items.text: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
items.hint: An easy pace. Same voice from start to finish.

items.text: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.
items.hint: Keep each day in your practised voice.

items.text: January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December.
items.hint: Twelve in a row: notice if the voice drifts by the end.

items.text: Fifty, fifty-one, fifty-two … all the way to seventy-five.
items.hint: Longer: take a breath whenever you need one.

levels.title: Everyday phrases
levels.subtitle: Short things you really say
levels.basis: NHS Fife: practise short phrases you actually use in real life. Swap in your own.
levels.written_by: Written by Lilt in the style of the source's examples.

items.text: Black coffee, please.
items.hint: Let the rise and fall follow the meaning.

items.text: Hi, it's me! Are you free later?
items.hint: Friendly and natural, not performed.

items.text: Good morning. How are you today?
items.hint: A real greeting, as if someone is there.

items.text: Could I have the bill, please?
items.hint: Polite and easy.

items.text: Thank you so much, that's lovely.
items.hint: Warm, without forcing it higher.

items.text: Hello, who's calling?
items.hint: Like answering the phone.

levels.title: Smooth sentences
levels.subtitle: Lots of m, n, l and vowels
levels.basis: Lilt's choice: sentences rich in voiced sounds (m, n, l, w and vowels) keep the voice going without breaks, which makes it easier to hear and keep your resonance. This is reading material, not a separate technique.

items.text: My mother made lemon meringue on Monday morning.
items.hint: Keep the buzz forward on every m.

items.text: We were walking along the river in the evening.
items.hint: One smooth line from start to finish.

items.text: Emily loves warm rolls with honey and lime.
items.hint: Light and easy.

items.text: I'm meeting Lena near the main library at noon.
items.hint: Natural rise and fall.

items.text: All along the lane, yellow leaves were swirling in the wind.
items.hint: Let it flow.

items.text: Many lovely melodies are made of only a few notes.
items.hint: Notice the m's and l's.

levels.title: Short passages
levels.subtitle: A paragraph to read aloud
levels.basis: NHS Fife progression includes reading short sentences and then several paragraphs aloud.

items.text: Every Saturday morning, I walk down to the little market by the river. The air smells of warm bread and fresh lemons, and everyone seems to be in a good mood. I usually buy honey from the same woman, who always remembers my name. Then I find a bench in the sun, open my notebook, and let the morning move slowly around me.
items.hint: Read at an easy pace. Breathe at the commas.

items.text: The rain started just after lunch, light at first and then heavier. I made a cup of tea, wrapped myself in a blanket, and listened to it drumming on the window. There was nowhere I needed to be. Sometimes the best afternoons are the ones where nothing happens at all, and the world feels a little quieter than usual.
items.hint: Keep your voice the same at the end of each sentence as at the start.

items.text: My neighbour has a tiny garden full of mint, lavender and tall yellow flowers. In the evening, when the light turns golden, she waters everything by hand and hums to herself. I once asked her what the song was. She laughed and said she had no idea; she just made it up as she went along, a little different every night.
items.hint: Notice where your voice drops; bring it back up gently.

levels.title: Your own words
levels.subtitle: Unscripted answers
levels.basis: NHS Fife progression moves on to speech that needs thinking about what you say, such as answering a question, then talking for a minute.

items.text: What did you do this morning?
items.hint: Answer in a few sentences, as if to a friend.

items.text: Describe the room you're in right now.
items.hint: No need to be clever: just describe it.

items.text: What's something you're looking forward to this week?
items.hint: Let your practised voice come along while you think.

items.text: Tell me about a place you love to go.
items.hint: Talk for up to a minute.

items.text: What would you cook for a friend tonight, and why?
items.hint: Relaxed and conversational.

items.text: What's a small thing that made you smile recently?
items.hint: Smile while you answer, if it feels natural.
